newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks up sharply in morning after Wall St jump.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks up sharply in morning after Wall St jump.

text.p: Property counters led Hong Kong stocks sharply higher on Thursday morning, with investors taking their cue from a strong overnight performance on Wall Street, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index was up 108.11 points, or 0.81 percent, at 13,518.87 after jumping to an early high of 13,568.86.
Turnover was HK$3.75 billion after the first hour of trade.
"It's mainly following the U.S. market overnight," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.

The Dow industrials rose 93.13 points on Wednesday to close at 6,945.85 after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan said the central bank was not out to deflate the stock market by boosting interest rates.
"A firm property market may aid sentiment here," Ng added.
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd rose HK$1.50 to HK$76.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd gained HK$1.00 to HK$91.50.

"If there is no move on interest rates, which I think is what the market has decided to think this morning, then the sorts of stocks that are running are property and the banks," said Julian Ings Chambers, assistant director at BZW Securities.
"They all stand to benefit from a reasonably benign interest rate outlook," he said.
Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc rose HK$2.50 to HK$190.50 and Hang Seng Bank Ltd gained HK$0.50 to HK$84.00.
But Ings Chambers said the market was not yet ready to break out of its range.
"I think you still need to see a significant pick up in institutional flows, and we still have not seen that," he said.
"I don't think there is much in the pipeline to kick start that again," Ings Chambers added.
Shares in Hongkong Telecom continued to rise on expectations of a share deal with a Chinese partner.
The stock was up HK$0.15 at HK$14.30 and among the busiest counters of the session.
"It is the last utility really that nothing significant has happened with over recent months in terms of ownership," said Ings Chambers.
